package_info.package_versions: All UI builds deployed to IPFS since January 1, 2024
package_info.why_malicious: A developer inserted malicious JavaScript into the Tornado Cash user interface, which covertly exfiltrated users’ private deposit notes to an external server, enabling theft of funds. This was a supply chain attack targeting users accessing the service via IPFS gateways.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user performs a deposit or withdrawal action in the Tornado Cash UI
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript code within the Tornado Cash web UI (served via IPFS gateways)
required_permissions: Access to in-browser cryptographic secrets (deposit notes) via UI event handlers

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user interacts with the Tornado Cash UI to perform a deposit or withdrawal, the code intercepts the user's private deposit note, encodes it, and sends it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled server, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive cryptographic secrets.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses sensitive cryptographic secrets (deposit notes) from user actions and transmits them to an external, attacker-controlled server, which is not required for legitimate Tornado Cash operations and directly enables theft of user funds.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Tornado Cash UI code should never transmit private deposit notes or cryptographic secrets off-device; all cryptographic operations and secret handling are expected to remain local to the user's browser. Any network transmission of such secrets is a clear violation of privacy and security expectations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate telemetry or analytics might send non-sensitive usage data (such as page views or error logs), but never private keys, deposit notes, or any cryptographic secrets. No legitimate use case exists for sending deposit notes to external servers.
key_indicators: Client-side JavaScript code accessing deposit notes or cryptographic secrets during user actions
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to external, non-Tornado Cash domains from the UI
Encoding of sensitive data (e.g., using encodeURIComponent or base64) prior to transmission
Presence of hardcoded external URLs or domains in UI source code not associated with official Tornado Cash infrastructure

attack_chain.action: A malicious developer submits a governance proposal containing backdoored JavaScript code to the Tornado Cash open-source repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is merged and deployed to IPFS gateways.

attack_chain.action: The compromised UI build is served to users via IPFS gateways (e.g., ipfs.io, cf-ipfs.com).
attack_chain.leads_to: Users interact with the malicious UI.

attack_chain.action: When users perform deposit or withdrawal actions, the malicious code captures their private deposit notes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive deposit notes are exfiltrated to the attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: The attacker collects exfiltrated deposit notes and uses them to withdraw or steal funds from Tornado Cash contracts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: theft of user funds and compromise of privacy.

behavioral_signatures: Client-side JavaScript accessing cryptographic secrets (deposit notes or private keys) during user deposit or withdrawal actions
Outbound network requests (e.g., HTTPS POST) from the UI to external domains not associated with Tornado Cash during normal user operations
Encoding and transmission of sensitive data (such as deposit notes) in network payloads, especially using encodeURIComponent or base64 encoding
file_indicators: Unexpected or obfuscated JavaScript code present in Tornado Cash UI builds deployed to IPFS
References to external domains or URLs not associated with official Tornado Cash infrastructure within UI source code (e.g., hardcoded attacker domains)
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests from user browsers running Tornado Cash UI to attacker-controlled domains (not tornado.cash or official infrastructure)
Unusual outbound traffic from IPFS-hosted Tornado Cash UIs to unknown or unlisted endpoints, especially during deposit or withdrawal actions
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Tornado Cash UI builds for unauthorized JavaScript code that accesses deposit notes or cryptographic secrets and transmits them to external servers. Use static and dynamic analysis to flag any code that reads sensitive secrets and initiates network requests to non-official domains. Implement network monitoring to alert on POST requests from Tornado Cash UIs to domains not on the official allowlist. Regularly audit governance proposals and code contributions for hidden or obfuscated data exfiltration logic, and verify that no cryptographic secrets are ever transmitted off-device.
